description: Iterates the source at 'delay'-second intervals until 'dur' is filled, filtering CUMULATIVELY through a user-defined resonator bank on every pass - early iterations sound like the source, later ones dissolve into pure tuned resonance. Pinned to submode 1 (filter pitches in Hz; submode 2 takes MIDI values with the same argv - verified working). The fbank parameter is an auxiliary text file (write_data_file()): one 'pitch amp' pair per line ('440 1.0'); amps may be dB values ('-6dB'); ';' comment lines legal; pitch is CDP-enforced 0.1-22050 in the file itself ('frq (30000.000) on line 1 out of range (0.1 to 22050.0):file ...'). Refusals verbatim: 'Not enough values on line 1: file ...' / 'Too many values on line 1: file ...'. Duration: iterations start at multiples of delay strictly below dur, so outdur = last-onset + indur; the curated expression indur + dur - delay is EXACT when dur/delay is an integer (probed 3.5000 from dur 3/delay 0.5/indur 1) and under-predicts by less than one delay otherwise (worst observed +0.1 s at dur 5/delay 0.3). Deterministic with rand/pshift/ashift at 0 (two runs 1.2 s apart byte-identical); any of them > 0 makes the render CLOCK-SEEDED, UNSEEDABLE stochastic (fltpcon.c:87 initrand48() = srand(time(0)); no seed argv) - runs differ every second and collide within the same second. Mono and stereo accepted.
musical_use: The musically distinctive filter in the family: a pulse-train-to-resonance morph in one pass. Each iteration re-enters the (still-sounding) filter bank, so the source's identity decays into the bank's chord - tune the fbank file to a harmony and any percussive source becomes that harmony. delay is the key knob: very short (<0.05 s) gives granular pulsation fusing into a wash; 0.1-0.2 s gives rapid-fire pulses dissolving into ringing; longer than the input gives discrete filtered repeats with gaps. Q controls how fast the dissolve happens - under ~10 holds the source character, hundreds ring pure. Add pshift (a few semitones, breakpoint-rampable) for weaving detuned strands, ashift for dying-away textures, -e for exponential per-segment decay (strong pulsation), -n to disable normalisation (raw cumulative gain - watch levels, overload is not reported). Keep rand/pshift/ashift at 0 when you need a reproducible take; there is no seed.

fbank.description: REQUIRED auxiliary text file (write with write_data_file(); any extension except .brk): one 'pitch amp' pair per line, pitch in Hz (this submode), amp 0.001-10000 or dB ('-6dB' verified). ';' comments legal. Error surface verbatim in the entry description. Resolved against the session's data/ directory.

q.description: Filter tightness (CDP-enforced 0.001 to 10000, verbatim refusal probed both ends). High Q dissolves the source into pure resonance sooner. DIVERGENCE: afta8 marks Q breakpoint-capable, but the binary REFUSES brk files here ('Cannot read parameter 1 [...]: brkpnt_files not permitted.') - unlike userbank/varibank, iterated's Q is scalar-only.

gain.description: Overall gain in the filtering process (CDP-enforced 0.001 to 10000). Breakpoint refused ('Cannot read parameter 2').

delay.description: Average time between iterations (CDP range 0.000002 to 32767, verbatim from the 40000 refusal). LANDMINE: a literal 0 slips the range check and HANGS the binary (timeout-killed, empty output left behind) - keep it positive. Values longer than the input give separated repeats. Breakpoint refused ('Cannot read parameter 3').

dur.description: Minimum duration of the output - the runtime minimum is the INPUT duration ('Parameter[5] Value (1.500000) out of range (2.000000 to 32767.000000)' on a 2 s file; the curated min 1.0 is the 1 s probe floor, real floor = indur). Sets the iteration span; output ends indur after the last onset below dur. Breakpoint refused ('Cannot read parameter 4').

prescale.description: Gain on the INPUT to the filtering process. DIVERGENCE: banner says 'Range (0.0 - 1.0)' but the binary enforces -1.0 to 1.0 ('Parameter[6] Value (2.000000) out of range (-1.000000 to 1.000000)') - negative values legal (polarity inversion). 0.0 auto-divides input level by the max overlay count. Breakpoint refused ('Cannot read parameter 7').

rand.description: Randomisation of the delay times, 0 (none) to 1 (max, CDP-enforced). ANY value > 0 makes the render clock-seeded stochastic with NO seed flag (two -r0.5 runs 1.2 s apart differ in samples AND frame count); 0 is fully deterministic. Breakpoint refused ('Cannot read parameter 8').

pshift.description: Maximum random pitch shift of any segment in (possibly fractional) semitones. CDP-enforced 0 to 48 (banner's '>=0' and afta8's 0-100 are wrong: 'Parameter[8] Value (200.000000) out of range (0.000000 to 48.000000)'). Stochastic and unseeded when > 0 (also changes output length: segments resample shorter/longer). BREAKPOINT-CAPABLE (a 0->6 ramp rendered, exit 0) - the shift CEILING can evolve over time.

ashift.description: Maximum random amplitude reduction of any segment, 0 to 1 (CDP-enforced). Stochastic and unseeded when > 0. BREAKPOINT-CAPABLE (a 0->0.8 ramp rendered, exit 0).

double.description: Double filtering - steeper isolation (verified: changes the render, duration unchanged).

interp_off.description: Turn OFF interpolation during pitch shift (fast but dirty). NO-OP without pshift (verified byte-identical to the base render at pshift 0) - only meaningful with -p.

expdecay.description: Exponential decay added: each segment gets quieter before the next enters (verified: changes render, RMS drops 0.109 -> 0.019 on the probe settings - strong pulsation).

nonorm.description: Turns OFF normalisation: segments may grow or fall in level quickly; gain has more impact but overload is NOT reported (verified: changes render).

examples.description: Percussive source dissolving into an A-major resonance: pulses every 0.25 s over 6 s.
examples.expected_use:
First write_data_file('fb_A.txt', '220 1.0
277.2 0.7
330 0.7
440 0.5'). Deterministic (no rand/pshift/ashift); output = indur + 6 - 0.25.

examples.description: Weaving detuned strands: pitch-shift ceiling ramping up, exponential per-segment decay.
examples.expected_use: High-Q ringing with segments roaming up to 4 st by the end. Clock-seeded: every run differs, no seed exists.

known_issues: BUFFER LANDMINE (first-class): with the default CDP memory buffer the process FAILS on inputs longer than about 1.48 s at 44.1 kHz mono ('ERROR: INTERNAL ERROR: (Bug?)' + 'ERROR: Failed to read all of source file: readsamps_with_wrap()', exit 255; 1 s works, 2 s fails). The whole input must fit one internal buffer (FLTITER uses 4 buffers from the CDP_MEMORY_BBSIZE pool, default 1 MB). Setting CDP_MEMORY_BBSIZE=8000 in the environment fixes it (2 s mono and stereo then run clean). Stereo halves the sample ceiling. Keep sources short or raise the env var.
delay 0 HANGS the binary (slips the 0.000002 floor, timeout is the only guard, empty .wav left behind) - never map 0 through.

CLOCK-SEEDED STOCHASTIC, UNSEEDABLE: rand/pshift/ashift > 0 randomise via srand(time(0)) (fltpcon.c:87 initrand48(), osbind.c) with no seed argv slot - runs 1.2 s apart differ; runs launched within the same second would collide byte-identically (family trap, cf. modify shred). rand=pshift=ashift=0 is fully deterministic (verified byte-identical pair).

Duration model indur + dur - delay is exact (to 1 frame) when dur/delay is an integer; otherwise the true output is up to one delay LONGER (last onset = largest multiple of delay strictly below dur). rand > 0 additionally jitters the final onset. Duration row pinned at the integer-ratio point delay 0.5/dur 3/indur 1 -> 3.5000.
Q is NOT time-variable here despite afta8 marking it brk ('Cannot read parameter 1 [...]: brkpnt_files not permitted.'); only -p pshift and -a ashift accept breakpoint files.
prescale's real range is -1.0 to 1.0 (banner says 0-1); pshift's real range is 0-48 st (banner '>=0', afta8 0-100).
The fbank pitch column is range-checked inside the datafile at 0.1-22050 Hz, not the banner's '0Hz to srate/3'.
Submode 2 (MIDI pitch values in the fbank file) verified working with identical argv - separate triple, not curated; same file format with MIDI numbers in column 1.
